title: R Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: cat joins values and writes them out. A backslash-n adds a new line. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: cat writes the greeting and the newline escape included in it. Unlike print, cat does not add a new line unless you ask.

exercises.question: The <- arrow assigns a value to a name. Here pencils keeps the number 3. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The left arrow stores 3. cat receives the sum of that value and 2. Use a number without quotes for maths.

exercises.question: A vector is an ordered group of values. c combines values into a vector. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: c combines three values into one vector. cat separates displayed values with spaces. R positions start at 1, unlike many other languages.

exercises.question: Square brackets select values. Position 2 is the second item in R. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: R positions start at 1. pets[2] reads dog. Index zero gives an empty selection, not the first item.

exercises.question: R can apply arithmetic to each value in a vector. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The multiplication applies to every position: 2 becomes 4 and 3 becomes 6. Different vector lengths can cause recycling; check their lengths.

exercises.question: A logical test makes true-or-false values. Use them in brackets to keep matching numbers. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The test makes FALSE, TRUE, TRUE. Only the two true positions are kept. The filter must describe the values you intend to keep.

exercises.question: mean adds values and divides by their count. This is the average. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The sum is 12. Dividing by three items gives the mean 4. Missing values need an explicit plan, such as na.rm = TRUE.

exercises.question: NA marks a missing value. is.na detects it. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: is.na is true only at the missing position. sum counts that one true value. Do not compare with == NA; use is.na.

exercises.code:
books <- data.frame(title = c("Moon", "Sun"), pages = c(24, 30))
cat(books$pages, "\n")
exercises.question: A data frame stores columns of the same row count. Each column has a name. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The dollar operator selects the pages column with values 24 and 30. Keep all columns the same length.

exercises.question: function defines reusable steps. R returns its final expression. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The function binds n to 4. Its final expression returns 8. Remember to call the function with parentheses.

exercises.code:
score <- 8
if (score >= 5) { cat("Pass\n") } else { cat("Try again\n") }
exercises.question: if checks one true-or-false value. else chooses the other action. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The single score passes the rule, so the first cat runs. A whole vector is not one if condition; choose a single rule.

exercises.question: sort returns a vector in order from smallest to largest by default. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: sort returns the values in increasing order: 3, 5 and 8. sort returns a result; keep it if you want to reuse it.
